findings.issue: actions/checkout runs with the default persist-credentials: true, so the read-only GITHUB_TOKEN is written into .git/config for the rest of the job.
findings.evidence: No reachable path: workflow_dispatch only, no inputs, no third-party code beyond pinned first-party actions, permissions contents: read, and the job runs only repo code. Matches ci.yml.
findings.fix: Optional hygiene: add `with: persist-credentials: false` to the checkout step (here and in ci.yml in a later task, for consistency).

summary: No BLOCKER/MAJOR/MINOR. Only untrusted input is the playtest:million argv: parseMillionArgs accepts only --help and --hands, value must match ^[0-9]+$ and lie in 9..1e9 (huge digit strings become large Numbers and fail the bound), bad values are never echoed. Children are spawned with process.execPath and a fixed argv array built from integers from planShards (no shell, no interpolation, cwd fixed to repo root). Resource bounds: shard stdout is the playtest summary (first violation only plus per-invariant counts) so buffered output is bounded regardless of --hands; --hands 1e9 only costs CPU time for a local user who asked for it, and the workflow takes no inputs and runs the default 1,000,000 under a 30-minute timeout; concurrency capped at availableParallelism over 9 shards. Child report parsing uses anchored, non-backtracking regexes (no ReDoS). Workflow: workflow_dispatch with no inputs, permissions contents: read, actions pinned to the same full SHAs as ci.yml, no secrets referenced. No new dependencies. Fixed shard seeds are intended for determinism and are not security-relevant (no fairness to users).
